title: Meir 2007: intraoperative disc hydrostatic pressure, anaesthetised lateral-lying patients (scoliotic vs non-scoliotic)
subcategory: thoracolumbar in vivo, intraoperative (no muscle load)
condition: general anaesthesia, lateral decubitus, anterior surgical approach (minimal muscle load)

quantity.name: IDP
quantity.definition: absolute hydrostatic nucleus pressure (MPa) where a hydrostatic region was found (horizontal = vertical stress for >= 2 consecutive 5 mm steps); mean +/- SD over discs

source.authors: Meir AR, Fairbank JCT, Jones DA, McNally DS, Urban JPG
source.sample: 11 patients (7 scoliotic: 25 discs; 4 non-scoliotic: 10 discs); 7 scoliosis patients (6F/1M, 13-25 y, Cobb 44-78 deg, thoracolumbar curves) and 4 non-scoliotic patients (4F, 15-40 y: 2 kyphosis, 2 discogenic LBP)

protocol.summary: Stress profilometry (side-mounted needle transducer, 1.33 mm) at 5 mm steps across exposed discs during anterior surgery, patients anaesthetised and lying laterally.
how_to_simulate: Lateral lying, no muscle activity (anaesthesia), no external load
Output: disc pressure from swelling/ligament tension only (a muscle-driven MSK model predicts ~0)
Use only as a lower-bound / baseline check of thoracolumbar IDP without loading

subject_model.per_patient: Meir 2007 Tables 1-2 (age, sex, diagnosis, curve type, Cobb angle, apical level, discs recorded); height/weight not reported

protocol.notes: Not an upright posture; mostly scoliotic discs. Informative baseline only.

data.x: scoliotic discs with a hydrostatic region (14/25 discs, 7 patients)
non-scoliotic: patient 10, L4/5 (discogenic LBP, 26 y F)
non-scoliotic: patient 8, T11/12 and L1/2 (kyphosis, 18 y F)
literature comparison (Yonezawa data, anaesthetised LBP patients, discs with hydrostatic nuclei 13/18)

extraction.from: Meir 2007 Results text p.6 and p.8-9 (Abstract: 0.25 vs <0.07 MPa)
extraction.check_notes: Re-read Results; patient 9 had no hydrostatic regions (mean vertical stress 0.327 +/- 0.33, horizontal 0.627 +/- 0.46 MPa over 4 discs) - not added as IDP.
